title: Diagnosing Prototype Estimation in Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning: Training-Free Geometry Selection and Unlabeled-Query Prototype Rectification

paper.title: Diagnosing Prototype Estimation in Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning: Training-Free Geometry Selection and Unlabeled-Query Prototype Rectification
paper.abstract:
Abstract Frozen visual encoders make prototype heads competitive in few-shot class-incremental
learning (FSCIL), but it remains unclear how much of the residual head gap is sensitive
to noisy novel-class means rather than to the subsequent changes introduced by
classifier refitting. On identical features, we construct a retrospective matched
counterfactual: first replace each five-shot novel mean with its complete-data
counterpart under fixed cosine scoring, then fit a linear probe. Across sixteen strong
encoder–dataset pairs, mean replacement accounts
for the majority of this ordered gap. Shot and classwise diagnostics support a
finite-sample mechanism, whereas a weaker base-only encoder does not satisfy the same
criterion. This diagnosis motivates ShrinkSel, a support-only selector over prototype radius and
covariance shrinkage whose family contains shared LDA as an exact fallback. Across
sixteen evaluated pairs, it improves LDA on fifteen by 0.04 0.04 – 1.52 1.52 points and
selects the exact LDA endpoint on Aircraft. We further introduce Query Prototype
Rectification ( QPR ), a
batch-transductive extension that uses gated unlabeled queries to update novel
directions while preserving the selected geometry. On CLIP ViT-B/16, QPR adds 1.21 1.21 – 2.03 2.03 points; exact query-wise self-exclusion retains the benefit, showing
that the gains do not require self-inclusion. The update repairs scarce novel prototypes at a measurable
base-class cost and weakens with plentiful supports or very small cohorts. Thus the
evidence available for prototype estimation is a central constraint in frozen-feature
FSCIL.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Few-shot class-incremental learning (FSCIL) must add new classes from a handful of labels without losing the base classes [ 27 , 39 ] . Most methods address representation drift or catastrophic forgetting [ 38 , 40 , 37 , 26 ] . Freezing a strong encoder prevents representation drift and parameter overwriting, yet all-seen performance can still decline through class competition. The resulting head is asymmetric: base classes have reliable statistics, while each novel class is represented by a noisy few-shot mean. We ask how much of the tested head gap is sensitive to this estimation error before a more flexible classifier is fitted. The answer depends on the information budget. As Fig. 1 shows, complete novel-class splits are used only for retrospective analysis. A support-only predictor may use frozen image features, base statistics, and labeled supports; a query-assisted predictor may additionally aggregate an unlabeled test cohort. Neither deployable path uses complete novel labels, text, or a known query-class marginal. We first construct an ordered matched counterfactual path: replace only the five-shot novel means under cosine scoring, then fit a linear probe to the same complete training features. Across sixteen strong CLIP, MAE-ft, and supervised ResNet settings, the first replacement accounts for most of this ordered gap. Increasing the shot count, measuring decision repairs, and relating prototype direction error to classwise loss support the finite-sample interpretation. Because a weaker base-only ResNet control does not show the same majority pattern, this is a bounded result for the tested representations and accounting order, not a universal law of FSCIL. The diagnosis suggests correcting geometry without fitting a fragile novel-class head. ShrinkSel selects among unit, raw, and bias-corrected prototype radii jointly with a pooled-covariance shrinkage path. Selection and a safety check use class-disjoint base episodes; cosine and shared-covariance LDA are endpoints, so the method can fall back exactly to LDA. When an unlabeled cohort is permitted, our new QPR operator admits confident novel-like queries and updates only novel directions, retaining the support-selected radius and metric. Query-wise self-exclusion tests whether the evaluated query itself is responsible for the update. Our contributions are: • a matched mean-versus-rule counterfactual path, with crossed uncertainty and empirical checks of the finite-shot mechanism; • ShrinkSel, a base-selected support-only geometry family with a conservative LDA fallback; and • QPR , our query-assisted estimator for cumulative all-seen transduction, evaluated with identity-disjoint calibration, query self-exclusion, and explicit cohort and base–novel trade-off checks. Together, the results show that scarce-class estimation is often more consequential than adding classifier flexibility, while also making clear that unlabeled-query repair is batch-dependent and not uniformly beneficial. Figure 1 : The analysis-only path first replaces five-shot novel means under fixed cosine scoring and then fits a complete-data linear probe. ShrinkSel selects support-only geometry from base classes; QPR adds a gated unlabeled-cohort update. Neither prediction path uses query labels or known class proportions.

sections.heading: FSCIL with fixed or adapted representations.
sections.text: FSCIL methods commonly modify the representation or classifier to preserve old classes and accommodate scarce new ones: CEC evolves classifiers, FACT reserves forward-compatible space, and NC-FSCIL, OrCo, and ASP impose geometric or prompt-based structure [ 38 , 40 , 37 , 1 , 15 ] . With strong pretrained features, however, simple fixed-feature heads can be competitive [ 34 ] . FSA limits adaptation to the first session, while RanPAC and RanDumb use analytic heads over fixed feature expansions [ 21 , 19 , 23 ] . We freeze the encoder in every session and isolate uncertainty in the resulting head.

sections.heading: Support-only estimation.
sections.text: Cosine NCM and prototypical networks represent a class by its support mean [ 20 , 25 ] . TEEN, Distribution Calibration, and higher-order calibration transfer base-class structure to scarce classes [ 31 , 36 , 6 ] ; EPT instead learns prototype offsets [ 10 ] . FeCAM and HyCal use covariance-aware distances, whereas ULA adjusts base–novel logits [ 5 , 13 , 33 ] . Distribution Calibration synthesizes features, higher-order calibration combines novel and semantically related base covariances after base-session adapter tuning, and EPT optimizes learned offsets. These are relevant calibration mechanisms but have different adaptation or synthetic data budgets from our fixed-feature closed-form head. ShrinkSel does not propose a new covariance estimator: it selects prototype radius jointly with classical covariance shrinkage [ 12 ] , using class-disjoint base episodes and retaining cosine and shared LDA as exact endpoints.

sections.heading: Different modality budgets.
sections.text: PriViLege, FDR, BiMC, TIM++, and Transductive CLIP use text, prompts, language-derived initialization, or vision–text probability features [ 22 , 35 , 3 , 14 , 18 ] . They provide important multimodal context but are not information-matched to our frozen image-only heads; the primary rankings therefore keep them separate.

sections.heading: Transductive inference.
sections.text: TIM optimizes mutual information, LaplacianShot enforces graph smoothness, PT-MAP uses optimal transport, and ProtoLP alternates propagation with prototype refinement [ 2 , 42 , 9 , 41 ] . These methods are usually studied in balanced, low-way, all-novel episodes and can depend on assumed query proportions [ 28 ] . Prototype Rectification also uses unlabeled queries, combining label propagation and feature shifting in episodic few-shot learning [ 16 ] ; we therefore do not claim the first use of unlabeled queries for prototype rectification. Our QPR targets the asymmetric all-seen FSCIL setting: many-shot base prototypes remain fixed, only gated novel directions move, the support-selected radius and metric are preserved, and no class marginal is provided.

sections.heading: Diagnosis.
sections.text: Approximation-risk analysis studies transfer, margins, and base–novel balance in FSCIL [ 32 ] . Our narrower question begins after the representation is fixed. An ordered counterfactual changes novel means and then classifier form on the same features, separating an estimation-sensitive term from a residual without claiming a unique causal decomposition.

sections.heading: 4.1 Experimental design
sections.text: We follow BiMC’s five-shot class orders and manifests [ 3 ] . CUB-200 uses 100 + 10 × 10 100+10\times 10 classes; CIFAR-100 and miniImageNet use 60 + 8 × 5 60+8\times 5 [ 30 , 11 , 29 ] . Aircraft and DTD provide additional domain checks [ 17 , 4 ] . Results average twenty matched support draws; the five-shot supports are nested in a K ∈ { 1 , 2 , 5 , 10 , 20 } K\in\{1,2,5,10,20\} study. The primary matrix uses frozen OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16, ViT-B/32, and RN50 image features [ 24 ] ; MAE-ft ViT-B/16 and supervised ImageNet ResNet-50 test cross-family transfer [ 7 , 8 ] . A ResNet-18 trained only on each benchmark’s base classes is a weaker class-disjoint control. The released encoders do not establish pretraining novelty, so all claims concern classes new to the head. Support-only comparisons include NCM, shared/diagonal LDA, TEEN, ULA, FeCAM, RanPAC, RanDumb, and an image-only reduction of HyCal [ 20 , 31 , 33 , 5 , 19 , 23 , 13 ] . Query-assisted comparisons use TIM-GD, LaplacianShot, ProtoLP, and uniform-marginal MAP-OT u [ 2 , 42 , 41 , 9 ] . Every matched comparison shares features, supports, sessions, and queries. The primary metric is the unweighted mean of sample-weighted session accuracies, including session 0. Paired method intervals use 10,000 support resamples; the diagnostic crossed support–class intervals use 5,000 draws. Full metric, selection, provenance, and implementation details appear in the supplement.

Each row starts from five-shot cosine NCM at zero. The blue endpoint changes only novel means to complete-data means while preserving cosine scoring; the orange endpoint then changes to a linear probe trained on the same complete-data images. Arrows show this second ordered change, so a leftward arrow means that the probe underperforms complete-mean cosine. Whiskers are 95% two-way bootstrap intervals over supports and novel classes. The path is an accounting device, not a causal decomposition. The complete-mean endpoint passes half of the matched five-shot-to-probe gap in every row of Fig. 2 . Because features, base prototypes, candidate classes, and scoring remain fixed along the blue step, this pattern specifically localizes most of the ordered gap to scarce novel statistics. It is not simply evidence that more labeled data improve an arbitrary head. The same majority conclusion holds across the cross-family and Aircraft checks, giving sixteen strong-representation settings in total. The direction of the orange step changes across datasets. Its leftward orientation on CUB shows that a full-data linear rule is not consistently better than full-data cosine prototypes. Extra classifier flexibility therefore cannot be treated as an oracle once estimation is controlled; its value depends on how a representation arranges within- and between-class variation. This is why Eq. ( 3 ) is an ordered description rather than a causal partition. Three diagnostics in the supplement strengthen, but also delimit, this interpretation. Accuracy improves monotonically as nested supports reduce mean uncertainty, and complete means repair substantially more decisions than they harm. Prototype angular error is associated with classwise loss on the standard matrix, yet Aircraft breaks that classwise relationship despite a large aggregate replacement effect. Angle measures estimation error; whether it flips a label also depends on the nearest competing margin. The aggregate matched intervention is consequently the primary evidence, with shot and angle trends serving as mechanism checks.

CIFAR instead eliminates most shrinkage choices because at least one class-disjoint fold regresses, while miniImageNet retains a short plateau among corrected-radius choices near the covariance endpoint. The selected cell is therefore determined jointly by mean performance and worst-fold safety, not by a smooth universal optimum. Target-oracle and leave-one-fold-out diagnostics in the supplement reach the same conclusion: discrete parameters can change while accuracy barely does. We claim transfer of audited performance, not recovery of a unique shrinkage coefficient. Novel-order permutations retain the qualitative result but do not vary the base/novel identity split. The supplement also compares matched image-only adapters and joint probes. Ordinary sample-weighted optimization is dominated by abundant replayed base examples, so it can strengthen the base block while leaving the five-example novel estimate poor. Inverse-frequency weighting shifts this balance and can reverse the overall ranking when base performance carries sufficient sample weight, but it still does not remove the novel-data bottleneck uniformly. These controls show why “optimized” is not an information-matched upper bound on a closed-form scarce-class head.

sections.heading: 4.5 Boundary and cost checks
sections.text: The base-only ResNet-18 control does not pass the majority criterion on any standard dataset. Because representation strength and pretraining exposure change together, this bounds the diagnosis without identifying which factor is responsible. Resource profiling on cached ViT-B/16 features shows that ShrinkSel stores one pooled eigensystem and class prototypes and adds novel means in closed form. These numbers, reported in the supplement, support a lightweight-head claim after feature extraction, not an end-to-end latency claim. QPR remains cohort-dependent regardless of its small head state.

sections.heading: 5 Limitations
sections.text: Our released encoders establish novelty only at the incremental head. CLIP’s corpus cannot be audited, and the additional encoder families use ImageNet supervision. The base-only ResNet control excludes novel benchmark classes but is also weaker, so it cannot separate exposure from representation quality. The complete-data means and linear probe are retrospective references. Their accounting is exact for the chosen order, but the two terms are descriptive rather than causal. ShrinkSel is a conservative combination of classical estimators; some gains over LDA are practically small, its selector only approximates cumulative novel competition, and transfer is conditioned on a fixed base/novel identity split. QPR is batch transductive, not an online or support-only method. Other cohort queries remain available even under query-wise self-exclusion, and moving novel prototypes can harm base predictions.

sections.heading: 6 Conclusion
sections.text: Matched counterfactuals across strong frozen representations identify novel-mean replacement as the larger component of the tested ordered head gap. This diagnosis motivates two deliberately bounded corrections: ShrinkSel selects support-only radius and covariance geometry with an exact LDA fallback, while the new QPR method uses an unlabeled cohort to repair novel directions without changing that geometry. Their behavior shows that frozen-feature FSCIL is governed less by a universally superior classifier than by which evidence is available to estimate each scarce class reliably.

Md Akib Haider * Md Hasanul Kabir Affiliation: Islamic University of Technology Affiliation: {tanvirhossain3, akibhaider, hasanul}@iut-dhaka.edu Abstract Frozen visual encoders make prototype heads competitive in few-shot class-incremental learning (FSCIL), but it remains unclear how much of the residual head gap is sensitive to noisy novel-class means rather than to the subsequent changes introduced by classifier refitting. On identical features, we construct a retrospective matched counterfactual: first replace each five-shot novel mean with its complete-data counterpart under fixed cosine scoring, then fit a linear probe. Across sixteen strong encoder–dataset pairs, mean replacement accounts for the majority of this ordered gap. Shot and classwise diagnostics support a finite-sample mechanism, whereas a weaker base-only encoder does not satisfy the same criterion. This diagnosis motivates ShrinkSel, a support-only selector over prototype radius and covariance shrinkage whose family contains shared LDA as an exact fallback. Across sixteen evaluated pairs, it improves LDA on fifteen by 0.04 0.04 – 1.52 1.52 points and selects the exact LDA endpoint on Aircraft. We further introduce Query Prototype Rectification ( QPR ), a batch-transductive extension that uses gated unlabeled queries to update novel directions while preserving the selected geometry. On CLIP ViT-B/16, QPR adds 1.21 1.21 – 2.03 2.03 points; exact query-wise self-exclusion retains the benefit, showing that the gains do not require self-inclusion. The update repairs scarce novel prototypes at a measurable base-class cost and weakens with plentiful supports or very small cohorts. Thus the evidence available for prototype estimation is a central constraint in frozen-feature FSCIL. 1 Introduction Few-shot class-incremental learning (FSCIL) must add new classes from a handful of labels without losing the base classes [ 27 , 39 ] . Most methods address representation drift or catastrophic forgetting [ 38 , 40 , 37 , 26 ] . Freezing a strong encoder prevents representation drift and parameter overwriting, yet all-seen performance can still decline through class competition. The resulting head is asymmetric: base classes have reliable statistics, while each novel class is represented by a noisy few-shot mean. We ask how much of the tested head gap is sensitive to this estimation error before a more flexible classifier is fitted. The answer depends on the information budget. As Fig. 1 shows, complete novel-class splits are used only for retrospective analysis. A support-only predictor may use frozen image features, base statistics, and labeled supports; a query-assisted predictor may additionally aggregate an unlabeled test cohort. Neither deployable path uses complete novel labels, text, or a known query-class marginal. We first construct an ordered matched counterfactual path: replace only the five-shot novel means under cosine scoring, then fit a linear probe to the same complete training features. Across sixteen strong CLIP, MAE-ft, and supervised ResNet settings, the first replacement accounts for most of this ordered gap. Increasing the shot count, measuring decision repairs, and relating prototype direction error to classwise loss support the finite-sample interpretation. Because a weaker base-only ResNet control does not show the same majority pattern, this is a bounded result for the tested representations and accounting order, not a universal law of FSCIL. The diagnosis suggests correcting geometry without fitting a fragile novel-class head. ShrinkSel selects among unit, raw, and bias-corrected prototype radii jointly with a pooled-covariance shrinkage path. Selection and a safety check use class-disjoint base episodes; cosine and shared-covariance LDA are endpoints, so the method can fall back exactly to LDA. When an unlabeled cohort is permitted, our new QPR operator admits confident novel-like queries and updates only novel directions, retaining the support-selected radius and metric. Query-wise self-exclusion tests whether the evaluated query itself is responsible for the update. Our contributions are: • a matched mean-versus-rule counterfactual path, with crossed uncertainty and empirical checks of the finite-shot mechanism; • ShrinkSel, a base-selected support-only geometry family with a conservative LDA fallback; and • QPR , our query-assisted estimator for cumulative all-seen transduction, evaluated with identity-disjoint calibration, query self-exclusion, and explicit cohort and base–novel trade-off checks. Together, the results show that scarce-class estimation is often more consequential than adding classifier flexibility, while also making clear that unlabeled-query repair is batch-dependent and not uniformly beneficial. Figure 1 : The analysis-only path first replaces five-shot novel means under fixed cosine scoring and then fits a complete-data linear probe. ShrinkSel selects support-only geometry from base classes; QPR adds a gated unlabeled-cohort update. Neither prediction path uses query labels or known class proportions. 2 Related Work FSCIL with fixed or adapted representations. FSCIL methods commonly modify the representation or classifier to preserve old classes and accommodate scarce new ones: CEC evolves classifiers, FACT reserves forward-compatible space, and NC-FSCIL, OrCo, and ASP impose geometric or prompt-based structure [ 38 , 40 , 37 , 1 , 15 ] . With strong pretrained features, however, simple fixed-feature heads can be competitive [ 34 ] . FSA limits adaptation to the first session, while RanPAC and RanDumb use analytic heads over fixed feature expansions [ 21 , 19 , 23 ] . We freeze the encoder in every session and isolate uncertainty in the resulting head. Support-only estimation. Cosine NCM and prototypical networks represent a class by its support mean [ 20 , 25 ] . TEEN, Distribution Calibration, and higher-order calibration transfer base-class structure to scarce classes [ 31 , 36 , 6 ] ; EPT instead learns prototype offsets [ 10 ] . FeCAM and HyCal use covariance-aware distances, whereas ULA adjusts base–novel logits [ 5 , 13 , 33 ] . Distribution Calibration synthesizes features, higher-order calibration combines novel and semantically related base covariances after base-session adapter tuning, and EPT optimizes learned offsets. These are relevant calibration mechanisms but have different adaptation or synthetic data budgets from our fixed-feature closed-form head. ShrinkSel does not propose a new covariance estimator: it selects prototype radius jointly with classical covariance shrinkage [ 12 ] , using class-disjoint base episodes and retaining cosine and shared LDA as exact endpoints. Different modality budgets. PriViLege, FDR, BiMC, TIM++, and Transductive CLIP use text, prompts, language-derived initialization, or vision–text probability features [ 22 , 35 , 3 , 14 , 18 ] . They provide important multimodal context but are not information-matched to our frozen image-only heads; the primary rankings therefore keep them separate. Transductive inference. TIM optimizes mutual information, LaplacianShot enforces graph smoothness, PT-MAP uses optimal transport, and ProtoLP alternates propagation with prototype refinement [ 2 , 42 , 9 , 41 ] . These methods are usually studied in balanced, low-way, all-novel episodes and can depend on assumed query proportions [ 28 ] . Prototype Rectification also uses unlabeled queries, combining label propagation and feature shifting in episodic few-shot learning [ 16 ] ; we therefore do not claim the first use of unlabeled queries for prototype rectification. Our QPR targets the asymmetric all-seen FSCIL setting: many-shot base prototypes remain fixed, only gated novel directions move, the support-selected radius and metric are preserved, and no class marginal is provided. Diagnosis. Approximation-risk analysis studies transfer, margins, and base–novel balance in FSCIL [ 32 ] . Our narrower question begins after the representation is fixed. Because representation strength and pretraining exposure change together, this bounds the diagnosis without identifying which factor is responsible. Resource profiling on cached ViT-B/16 features shows that ShrinkSel stores one pooled eigensystem and class prototypes and adds novel means in closed form. These numbers, reported in the supplement, support a lightweight-head claim after feature extraction, not an end-to-end latency claim. QPR remains cohort-dependent regardless of its small head state. 5 Limitations Our released encoders establish novelty only at the incremental head. CLIP’s corpus cannot be audited, and the additional encoder families use ImageNet supervision. The base-only ResNet control excludes novel benchmark classes but is also weaker, so it cannot separate exposure from representation quality. The complete-data means and linear probe are retrospective references. Their accounting is exact for the chosen order, but the two terms are descriptive rather than causal. ShrinkSel is a conservative combination of classical estimators; some gains over LDA are practically small, its selector only approximates cumulative novel competition, and transfer is conditioned on a fixed base/novel identity split. QPR is batch transductive, not an online or support-only method. Other cohort queries remain available even under query-wise self-exclusion, and moving novel prototypes can harm base predictions. 6 Conclusion Matched counterfactuals across strong frozen representations identify novel-mean replacement as the larger component of the tested ordered head gap.
